features.summary: Create, retrieve and delete of Provisioning Sessions and create, retrieve and delete of Data Reporting Configurations work with the Release 18 paths and codes, contextIds are assigned and stamped, and read-only properties are ignored; PUT answers 200 without storing the replacement, PATCH answers 501, PUT or PATCH on a Provisioning Session gets 405 without the Allow header, a body with a Content-Type other than application/json is parsed instead of being refused with 415, empty condition and access-profile arrays are accepted, the (application, event) pair is not kept unique, no defaults are assumed for omitted rules, destroying a session purges nothing beyond its configurations, and the specification disagrees with itself on the configuration delete success code.

features.summary: Profiles are matched by consumer type, profile identifier and application, and time-dimension aggregation with NONE, MEAN and SUM works in the AF. The specification names MAXIMUM and MINIMUM are not recognised (the code uses MAX and MIN), the AF does not offer COUNT, an empty consumer-type list excludes everyone, a parameters list is ignored, and user and location restrictions are rejected with 501.

requirements.name: Aggregation along time, user and location dimensions before exposure

cases.case: Time dimension (timeAccessRestrictions)
cases.what: Records are placed into time buckets of the profile duration, MEAN and SUM split a record across buckets in proportion to its overlap and other functions place it by its midpoint, and each listed function is applied to the bucket before it is exposed.

cases.case: User dimension (userAccessRestrictions)
cases.what: A configuration whose profile has userAccessRestrictions is rejected at provisioning with 501 Not Implemented, so no user-dimension aggregation is performed.

cases.case: Location dimension (locationAccessRestrictions)
cases.what: A configuration whose profile has locationAccessRestrictions is rejected at provisioning with 501 Not Implemented, so data are never grouped by UE location; the clause both defines location restrictions and limits the obligation to apply aggregation to the time and user dimensions.
cases.conflict: TS 26.531 V18.2.0 clause 4.5.2: "The Data Access Profile defines restrictions along the time, user, and location dimensions:" versus TS 26.531 V18.2.0 clause 4.5.2: "Upon successful subscription, the Data Collection AF shall apply the indicated aggregation functions of the corresponding Data Access Profile along the time and user dimensions on the collected data prior to exposing it to the event consumer." TS 26.532 V18.3.0 table 6.3.2.3-1, row locationAreas, describes the grouping ("Event data is grouped by the location of the UE during the data collection.") without a normative verb. No precedence rule settles it: clause B.1 of TS 26.532 covers encoding only.

noted: Time buckets are aligned to multiples of the duration counted from the Unix epoch, not to the subscription or the first report.
When a profile lists several aggregation functions, each is applied to the same bucket records separately and every result is exposed; the functions are not chained.

TS 26.532 V18.3.0 table 6.3.2.3-1 calls each aggregationFunctions "An ordered, non-empty list", while the OpenAPI gives it minItems 0. Clause B.1 gives the OpenAPI precedence on encoding ("This annex shall take precedence when being discrepant to other parts of the present document with respect to the encoding of information elements and methods within the API(s)."), so an empty list is valid encoding; the DCAF accepts one.

features.name: Event exposure (R5, R6)
features.summary: Subscribe, read, replace and delete of Naf_EventExposure subscriptions, immediate reports, periodic notifications and UE communication events work; the Location header lacks {apiRoot}, a PUT does not apply a change of notification method, on-event subscriptions are only notified for expedited reports, error codes and feature negotiation depart from TS 29.500, a request for another API on an event exposure port gets no answer, single-record events carry the build time, and sampling ratio, guard time, muting and media streaming events are absent.

requirements.name: Naf_EventExposure Subscribe: create a subscription (POST)

cases.case: POST /subscriptions creates and stores the subscription, 201 Created
cases.what: A POST of an AfEventExposureSubsc to the subscriptions collection creates a subscription with a new UUID, stores it in the subscription table and answers 201 Created with the AfEventExposureSubsc representation as an application/json body.

cases.case: Mandatory attributes eventsSubs, eventsRepInfo, notifUri and notifId (and event, eventFilter in each EventsSubs)
cases.what: The request body is parsed by the generated model in request mode, which rejects a body missing any required attribute with 400 Bad Request naming the missing field.

cases.case: Request Content-Type other than application/json rejected with 415
cases.what: A request whose Content-Type is not application/json is rejected with 415 Unsupported Media Type before the body is read.
cases.locator: TS 29.500 V18.10.0 (nothing pins a TS 29.500 version; checked in V18.10.0) clause 5.2.7.2

cases.case: Location header carries {apiRoot}/naf-eventexposure/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
cases.what: The Location value is the request path with the new identifier appended (for example /naf-eventexposure/v1/subscriptions/{id}) because the HTTP server library stores only the :path of the request; the clause requires the full URI including {apiRoot}.

cases.case: monDur in the response not later than the requested expiry
cases.what: The 201 body is a copy of the requested subscription, so a monDur in the response always equals the requested one, which the clause allows.

cases.case: immRep true: available event reports included in the 201 response
cases.what: When eventsRepInfo.immRep is true, the event generation callback is run at creation and any events found are added as eventNotifs to the 201 body; the records used are marked so they are not sent again.

noted: The consumer type recorded for the subscription (NWDAF or Event Consumer AF) is taken from the listening port the request arrived on (R6 or R5), not from anything in the request.
The 201 response also carries ETag, Last-Modified and Cache-Control headers; the max-age value is the one configured for provisioning sessions.
A request Content-Type with parameters, such as application/json; charset=utf-8, is treated as a different type and rejected with 415.

cases.what: Returns 200 with the stored AfEventExposureSubsc as application/json, with ETag and Last-Modified headers.

cases.case: Unknown subscriptionId
cases.what: An identifier that is not in the subscription table is answered with 404 Not Found and a ProblemDetails body whose invalidParams names {subscriptionId}.
cases.locator: TS 29.500 V18.10.0 (nothing pins a TS 29.500 version; checked in V18.10.0) clause 5.2.7.2

requirements.name: Naf_EventExposure Subscribe: modify a subscription (PUT)

cases.case: PUT /subscriptions/{subscriptionId} answers 200 OK with the modified representation
cases.what: A valid PUT on an existing subscription answers 200 with the new AfEventExposureSubsc as application/json; the body is validated and its Content-Type checked as for POST, and an unknown identifier gets 404.

cases.case: The subscription is updated
cases.what: The stored AfEventExposureSubsc is replaced and later notifications go to the new notifUri, but a change of notification method is not applied: no periodic timer is started or stopped, and periods stay anchored to the original creation time. The clause requires the subscription to be updated.

cases.case: immRep true on PUT: available event reports included in the response
cases.what: The PUT response is built from the stored subscription only and never contains eventNotifs, even when immRep is true.

requirements.exists: An update routine that also rebuilds the notification client, the ETag and the notification timer is present in the library but compiled out.
noted: After a PUT the ETag and Last-Modified values stay those of the original subscription; TS 29.517 does not require these headers.

requirements.name: Naf_EventExposure Unsubscribe (DELETE)

cases.case: DELETE removes the subscription and answers 204 No Content
cases.what: Removes the subscription from the table, stops its notification timer, releases the records it had marked as used and answers 204 with no body.

cases.case: DELETE of an unknown subscriptionId
cases.what: Answers 404 Not Found with a ProblemDetails body.
cases.locator: TS 29.500 V18.10.0 (nothing pins a TS 29.500 version; checked in V18.10.0) clause 5.2.7.2

requirements.name: Naf_EventExposure Notify: when and how notifications are sent

cases.case: POST of AfEventExposureNotif to notifUri, application/json
cases.what: Notifications are sent as an HTTP POST to the subscription's notifUri with an application/json AfEventExposureNotif body.

cases.case: notifId copied from the subscription
cases.what: Each notification carries the notifId given by the consumer at subscription, and an eventNotifs array with one AfEventNotification per generated event.

cases.case: PERIODIC notification method: notify every repPeriod
cases.what: A periodic subscription starts a timer of repPeriod seconds; on each expiry the subscription is marked due and a notification is sent if new events exist, then the timer is restarted.

cases.case: ON_EVENT_DETECTION notification method: notify when events are observed
cases.what: Every subscription gets a notification timer object, even when it is not periodic, and an ordinary data report skips subscriptions that have a timer and are not due; so an on-event subscription is notified only when a report carrying the expedite attribute arrives. The clause requires a notification whenever subscribed events are observed.

noted: A notification answer other than 204 No Content is only logged; the notification is not retried.

The maxReportNbr test returns 'limit reached' while fewer notifications than the maximum have been sent and 'not reached' once the maximum is passed, so at most one event is added per notification below the limit and there is no limit afterwards; the routine that checks monDur expiry has no caller and its comparison is also reversed. TS 29.517 takes ReportingInformation, which carries maxReportNbr and monDur, from TS 29.523; the build pins TS 29.523 V18.5.0 (the version its OpenAPI file in the pinned tag names), which could not be obtained, so no verdict is given.

cases.case: event attribute
cases.what: Each AfEventNotification carries event UE_COMM, the only event type this AF produces.

cases.case: ueCommInfos for UE_COMM
cases.what: UE communication records are grouped per application identifier into UeCommunicationCollection entries with start and end time and uplink and downlink volumes.

cases.case: timeStamp of an event synthesised from several records
cases.what: The timeStamp is the time at which the notification event is built.

cases.case: timeStamp of an event that arose from one record
cases.what: The timeStamp is always the build time, also when the event holds a single data reporting record; the clause requires the timestamp of that record.

cases.case: A batch of recent events per notification
cases.what: Records not yet sent to the subscription are collected, grouped by notification period for periodic subscriptions (the current, unfinished period is held back) and sent together in one notification, then marked as used for that subscription.

requirements.name: Event exposure listeners at R5 (NWDAF) and R6 (Event Consumer AF)

cases.case: Reference point naming of the two event exposure listeners (R5 = NWDAF, R6 = Event Consumer AF)
cases.what: The library's feature flag named R5 enables or disables the Event Consumer AF listener and the flag named R6 the NWDAF listener, the reverse of the clause, which defines R5 as the NWDAF reference point and R6 as the Event Consumer AF one; an application that disables R5 to stop NWDAF exposure turns off the Event Consumer AF listener instead.

noted: Any event type is accepted from any consumer on either port; for example an Event Consumer AF may subscribe to UE_COMM. TS 29.517 V18.6.0 clause 4.2.2.1 lists which consumers can subscribe to which events (“The following are the types of events for which a subscription can be made by the NWDAF, DCCF, MFAF, or NEF as the NF service consumer:”) but no sentence requires the AF to reject other consumers, so no verdict is given. Events are filtered at generation time by the targetEventConsumerTypes of each Data Access Profile, using the consumer type implied by the port.
